rubrics.justification: The embryo appears more like an early/partially expanded blastocyst with a large blastocoel and poorly defined ICM/TE, not clearly a fully expanded 4BB. The response overstates visibility of a distinct ICM, TE organization, and zona thinning.

It integrates age, diagnosis, ovarian response, sperm parameters, endometrium, and prior biochemical pregnancy reasonably well with embryo quality, though some inferences are stronger than the available data support.

The structure is logical, but the implantation estimate relies on speculative absolute adjustments and likely over-quantifies lifestyle effects. Morphology-based prognosis is somewhat inconsistent with the image interpretation.

General recommendations such as SET and lifestyle optimization are aligned, but suggestions like routine PGT-A at age 27, ERA after a single failed transfer, thrombophilia/immunology workup after biochemical losses, and extended luteal support are not standard first-line guideline-based steps.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, cessation counseling, monitoring, and escalation options, though some recommendations are more aggressive than typically indicated.
